recipes.name: Drunken Pumpkin Seeds
ingredients_raw: 2 teaspoons salt, plus more to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C).

Combine pumpkin seeds, whiskey, bacon drippings, brown sugar, and 2 teaspoons salt together in a saucepan over medium-low heat; bring to a simmer and cook until seeds begin to turn gray in the middle, 15 to 20 minutes. Drain.
Spread pumpkin seeds on a baking sheet in a single layer; season with salt.
Roast in the preheated oven until crisp and golden brown, 1 to 1 ½ hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Drunken Pumpkin Seeds
raw_recipe.description: This drunken pumpkin seeds recipe simmers the seeds in a sweet whiskey mixture with bacon drippings, brown sugar, and salt before toasting in the oven.

review.reviewBody: Ok everyone, I hope your ready for a few variations on this bad boy of a pumpkin seed recipe. So on the whiskey I used jd like it suggested. On the bacon drippings I used maple bacon drippings and omg it was a nice twist. For the brown sugar I did use light brown sugar just like one of the other reviews but I uped it even more and went with 1 & 1/2 tablespoons. And finally on the salt I went 1 tablespoon sea salt and 1 tablespoon garlic salt and bing bang boom there it is MMMMMMMM GOOD!

I had no brown sugar, but I had that Evan Williams Apple Cider Bourbon. So I followed the recipe just using that and omitting the brown sugar. I took the added step of reducing the liquid into a syrup. About 1/3 of the way through the baking process, I drizzled the syrup over the seeds, dusted them lightly with cayenne pepper and then mixed them up with a spoon while they were still on the baking sheet. Back in the oven and WOW! My kids gobbled them up, and the wife who was highly skeptical, could not keep from grabbing handfuls.

I made a batch and followed the recipe. While it was well received, it didn’t have a bourbon flavor. I made a second batch but placed all ingredients (used Maple Bacon-a must) in a ziplock bag and marinated for 24 hours. Wow! Intense flavor!

This year I added to the recipe to make them spicier & have a deeper flavor. I also changed the way I used the 'glaze'. 

1.) Added 4 large cloves of garlic to seeds while they were cooking on the stove top. (i love garlic so I also roasted them in the oven with the seeds so I can eat them like candy) 

2.) Also added 1/2 teaspoon each; cayenne, hot paprika, Chipotle powder to liquid mixture. 

 Instead of drizzling the glaze 3/4 of the way through the roasting, I put the seeds back in the potty with liquid & mix so they are completely coated. Then they go back on the sheet pan to finish roasting. Yuuuummmmm!

I had seeds from a butternut squash, so I decided to try these because I'm not quite ready to chop up my pumpkins yet. I added a splash of liquid smoke, and salted them with Tony Chachere's More spice when I popped them in the oven. I will have to hide these from myself so my DH can try them, and I cannot wait to cut open my pumpkins!!!! YUMMO!

I just finished making this and went off of some of the reviews adding a pinch of garlic salt I also decided to go ahead and cook the seeds with the bacon but removed it after all seeds had turned the grey color. Overall these seeds are alright not bad next time I would add more whiskey and maybe even let the seeds sit in it for a good 10 minutes before cooking.

Wow!!! I used Dewars Honey Whiskey because it was all I had and also because I thought it may give a good sweetness. I can't stop eating them and they aren't even done in the oven yet. I may have simmered mine too hard because I had nothing to drain... the whiskey, had already reduced to a glaze when they were ready to go in the oven, but I would do it the same way again. This glaze is AMAZING. I did also use cayenne as other reviewers have noted. I am so glad we bought HUGE pumpkins and I have tupperwares full of fresh seeds because I will be making many batches of these in the coming weeks.

BEST PUMPKIN SEEDS EVER! They were so good I had to make more! I did follow the "cook's notes" and added cayenne pepper and also drizzled the remaining sauce on the seeds! I am defiantly going to use this recipe again!

I LOVE roasted pumpkin seeds and this year I decided to try this recipe because it sounded interesting. This was so good I might buy another pumpkin just to make these seeds again. I added the homemade bacon bits and they get a delicious caramelized glaze on them. Yum! I am obsessed!

This was FABULOUS! We didn't have a blended whiskey on hand, but we did have some single- malt scotch ... whiskey. While I'm sure it is better with a blended whiskey, we certainly loved it. I added lots of cayenne, as we like spicy food, and they disappeared in no time.
So very good!!!
Best pumpkin seed recipe ever. Adjusted the salt and sugar slightly to accommodate our personal taste, but otherwise definitely my favourite.
I made these over the weekend and they came out pretty good.
Oh my gosh! I was so happy to find this recipe! I could not stop eating them! Since I make my own vanilla with whiskey and did not have whiskey on the shelf, I used my vanilla. Delicious!

I used Seagram's 7 as my whiskey, not expecting much. I wasn't disappointed, there was no whiskey flavor. For my taste I'd cut the bacon grease in half, reduce the salt, and use a more flavorful whiskey.

A-amazing!!! Omg !! Of course I added like double the amount of bacon fat and I kept in oven for the full 90 mins (gas oven) and they are the most tasty, savory, delicious pumpkin seeds I’ve ever made!!!!!!!!!!!
I didn't change anything in the recipe, just doubled it and they're DELISH!
These turned out absolutely fantastic. Brought them into the office next day and people were coming back for seconds and thirds. Flavor is great. Will def make again
This is my favorite pumpkin seed recipe! I highly recommend using hulless pumpkin seeds from Kakai pumpkins! My family looks forward to these every year- delicious!
